AMENDMENT NO. 1 SEPTEMBER 1993 TO IS 1774:1986 SPECIFICATION FOR PAPER FOR PERMANENT AND SEMI-PERMANENT RECORDS
(First Revision) ( Page 3, clause 0.4) -- Add this new clause after clause 0.3 and renumber the subsequent clause: '0.4 A scheme for labelling envitonment friendly products known as ECO Mark has been introduced at the instance of the Ministry of Environment and Forests (MEF), Government of India. The ECO Mark would be administered by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) under the BIS Act, 1986 as per the Resolutions No. 71 dated 21 February 1991 and No. 425 dated 28 October 1992 published in the Gazette of the Government of India. For a product to be eligible for marking with ECO logo, it shall also carry the Mark of BIS besides meeting additional optional environment friendly requirements. For this purpose, the Standard Mark of BIS would be a single mark being a combination of the Mark and the ECO logo. Requirements to be satisfied for a product to qualify for the BIS Standard Mark for ECO friendliness, will be inlcuded in the relevant published Indian Standaids through an amendment. These requirements will be optional; manufacturing u n i t s will be free to opt for the Mark alone also. This amendment is based on the Gazette Notification No. 455 dated 13 November 1992 for paper as environment friendly products published in the Gazette of India. This amendment is, therefore, being issued to this standard to include environment friendly requiremente for paper for permanent and semi-permanent records.' ( Page 7, clause 5.7 ) -- Add the following new clause after 5.7: '5.8 Optional Requirements for ECO Mark 5.8.1 General Requirements 5.8.1.1 The product shall conform to the requirements for quality and performance prescribed under clauses 5.1 to 5.7. 5.8.1.2 The manufacturer shall produce to BIS, the environmentel consent clearance from the concerned State Pollution Control Board as per the provisions of Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 and Air (Prevention and Control of Polution) Act, 1981 along with the authorisation, if required, under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and the rules made thereunder, while applying for ECO Mark.

1

5.8.2 Specifie Requirements 5.8.2.1 The material shall be of the following two types depending on the raw material used in the manufacture: a) Type A -- Manufactured from pulp containing not less than 60 percent by mass of pulp made from materials other than bamboo, hard woods, soft wooda and reed. b) Type B -- Manufactured from pulp made from 100 percent waste paper.' ( Page 7, clause 6.1 ) -- Add the following new clause after 6.1: '6.1.1 For ECO Mark, the product shall be packed in such packages which shall be recyclable/reusable or biodegradable.' ( Page 7, clause 6.2 ) -- Add the following new clause after 6.2.1: '6.2.2 For ECO Mark, following additional information may also be marked on the container/package: The criteria for which the product has been labelled with ECO Mark.'

IS : 1774 - 1986

Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR PAPER FOR PERMANENT AND SEMI-PERMANENT RECORDS

( First Revision )
0. F O R E W O R D
0.1 This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 1 April 1986, after the draft finalized by the Paper and Its Products (Excluding Packaging Materials ) Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 This standard was originally published in 1961 at the request of the National Archives of India to ensure proper quality of paper for use by concerned agencies and was based on data obtained from the National Archives of India, New Delhi, Handmade Paper Research Centre, Pune and the Forest Research Institute, Dehra Dun. It covered only one type of paper meant for permanent records. 0.3 Having noted that paper meant for records are primarily of three types, namely: (a) paper meant for use for records expected to last several hundred years, (b) paper meant for use for records expected to last in excess of 100 years, and (c) paper meant for use for records expected to last at least 50 and up to 100 years, the Sectional Committee undertook the present revision to include these three types of paper. The present revision also takes into consideration paper used in records meant for ordinary use and in records meant for frequent reference. Normally, for these types of records, bond and ledger papers are used and these are covered in this specification. In preparing this standard, the Committee has given due consideration to the views of producers, consumers and technologists. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.
*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ).

3

IS : 1774 - 1986
1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard covers the requirements and methods of sampling and test for paper meant for use for permanent and semi-permanent records. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.0 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in IS : 46611986* and the following shall apply. 2.1 Alkali Filled Paper -- A paper containing calcium or magnesium carbonate or both. Such papers are alkaline with p H range between 7.5 to 9.5, and contains reserve buffering capacity that can neutralise acidic gases that may be absorbed from the atmosphere. 2.2 Durability -- The ability of a paper to resist the effects of wear and tear encountered during actual use. 2.3 High Referral Grade -- The grade of paper meant for use in records which are frequently handled. 2.4 Neutralized Paper -- A paper that has been sized with a rosinalum system in which sodium aluminate has been substituted for part of the alum that normally is used or with one of the synthetic sizes such as ketone dimer or acrylic emulsions. 2.5 P e r m a n e n c e -- This basically is a function of the chemical stability of the paper and its ability to maintain initial properties over a long period of time. Permanence is further defined with respect to the end use as follows. 2.5.1 Maximum Permanence -- T h e paper is expected to last several hundred years. 2.5.2 High Permanence -- T h e paper is expected to last in excess of 100 years. 2.5.3 Semi-permanence -- The paper is expected to last at least 50 years and up to 100 years. 3. TYPES 3.1 The paper shall be of three types, depending on the p H of paper and/or type of filler/sizing agent used as below: Tpye 1 -- Paper with maximum permanence presence of alkaline filler. characterized by

*Glossary of terms used in paper trade and industry ( first revision ). 4

IS : 1774 - 1986 Type 2 -- Paper with high permanence characterized by neutral p H condition of the paper. Type 3 -- Paper with semi-permanence characterized by pH value of paper not below 5.5. 4. GRADES 4.1 Each type of paper shall be of two grades depending on its usage as indicated below: Grade 1 -- Ordinary use, and Grade 2 -- High referral, characterized by higher tearing resistance and folding endurance. 5. REQUIREMENTS 5.1 F u n u s h -- When tested according to IS : 5285-1969* the paper shall be made from fully bleached pulps and will preferably contain varying percentage of cotton, hemp or softwood fibres or a mixture of these as agreed to between the buyer and the supplier and shall be free from unbleached pulps or ground wood. 5.2 Finish -- The grain of the paper shall be in the machine or cross direction as agreed to between the buyer and the supplier. 5.3 Sizing -- The paper shall be suitably internal or surface sized or both so that it shall be suitable for the intended purpose as indicated by the buyer. Visible feathering shall not be apparent after the paper has been written on with the aqueous ink, erased and again written on the erased area with aqueous ink. If the paper is to be used in a printing process, the paper shall be suitable for this purpose. 5.4 The paper for permanent records shall also comply with the requirements given in Table 1, when tested according to the methods indicated in col 9 to 11 of the table. 5.5 Accelerated A g e i n g -- The paper shall be subjected to accelerated ageing by heating in an oven maintained at 103 � 2�C for 72 hours, at the end of which the paper shall retain at least 50 percent of its original folding endurance. 5.6 Size -- The paper shall be in the form of sheets. The sizes and tolerance on sizes shall be in accordance with IS : 1064-1980 unless otherwise agreed to between the buyer and the supplier. *Methods of tests for fibre analysis of paper and board. Specification for paper sizes (second revision). 5

IS : 1774 - 1986 5.7 Colour -- The paper shall be white or coloured as agreed to between the buyer and the supplier. 6. PACKING AND MARKING 6.1 Packing -- A ream of 500 sheets shall be a measure of quantity and the paper shall be securely and suitably packed as agreed to between the buyer and the supplier. 6.2 Marking -- Each package shall be marked with the following particulars: a) Description, type, grade and colour of the material; b) Size and substance of the material; c) Mass in kg per ream of sheets inculding wrapping paper; d) Lot number; e) Month and year of manufacture; and f) Manufacturer's name or recognized trade-mark; if any. 6.2.1 The package shall also be marked with the Standard Mark.
NOTE -- The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

7. SAMPLING 7.1 T h e paper shall be sampled in accordance with 3 of IS : 1060 ( Part 1 )-1966*. 8. CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 8.1 N u m b e r of Teat -- The test shall be conducted as given in IS : 1060 (Part 1)-1966*. 8.2 The test shall be declared as conforming to the requirements of this standard if all the test results meet the relevant requirements.
*Methods of sampling and test for paper and allied products, Part 1 ( revised ).

IS : 1774 - 1986

APPENDIX A [ Clause 5.4, Table 1, Sl No. (ii) ]
DETERMINATION OF ALKALINE FILLER MATERIAL CONTENT A-1 PROCEDURE A-1.1 Weigh approximately one gram of paper to the nearest 1 mg, making a correction for the moisture content ( Note 1 ) and place it in approximately 25 ml of water in a 125 ml Erlenmeyer flask. Pipette 20 ml (Note 2) of standard 0.1 N hydrochloric acid into the flask. Heat to boil (approximately one minute). Add 3 drops of aqueous methyl red. Cool to room temperature and titrate to the first lemon yellow colour with standard 0.1 N sodium hydroxide solution. A-1.2 If a trace of pink indicator remains absorbed on the surface of the paper, boil the paper briefly to desorb the pink colour. Usually a furtner drop of sodium hydroxide solution will restore the lemon yellow colour of the solution.
NOTE 1 -- The specimen for analysis may be dried and weighed or a separate protion may be used for moisture determination by the method given in 9 of IS : 1060 (Part 1)-1966*. NOTE 2 -- For one gram specimen; 20 ml of 0.1 N hydrochloric acid is sufficient to neutralize the carbonate in a paper containing approximately 10 percent carbonate.

A-2. CALCULATION A-2.1 Calculate the alkaline material content of the paper as percent calcium carbonate ( C a C O 3 ) as follows: Alkaline material content, percent by mass = where 0.05 is the milliequivalent mass of CaCO 3 . A-2.2 Duplicate determination should agree within 0.3 percent CaCO 3 . A-3. REPORT A-3.1 Report the carbonate content as percent CaCO 3 of the even dry paper, nearest to 0.1 percent.
*Methods of sampling and test for paper and allied products, Part 1 ( revised ).
